messages:
anya: hi all, anya here — first day. tried to trigger infra pipeline from my fork and got a weird mix of errors: Buildkite says I lack pipeline permissions and the container pull from GHCR is 403. who should I ping for onboarding perms?

rob: welcome! :wave: two separate things usually: Buildkite pipeline membership (Okta group) and GHCR access (org GitHub App or PAT). what's the exact Buildkite error?

anya: paste from the agent log:
```
Buildkite: ERROR: You do not have permission to restart this pipeline (requires membership in pipeline:infra).
Docker: failed to pull image "ghcr.io/redwood/ci-runner:stable": unauthorized: access to the requested resource is denied (403)
```

kevin: confirming: forks don't get the org GitHub App token and we lock pipeline restarts to the redwood-ci Okta group. lisa can add you to the group. we also avoid exposing org secrets to fork PRs in actions.

lisa: adding Anya to redwood-ci now. infra-bot will create the access ticket so ops can review.

infra-bot: Access request created: CI-9992 owner=lisa status=pending reviewers=[infra-oncall]

anya: thanks lisa. restarted build after accept/being added and now Buildkite allows restart but GHCR still 403.

rob: two options: 1) run the sensitive job in the upstream (open a PR and ask devs to run CI in the main repo), or 2) we can provision a short-lived restricted PAT/packages:read token for your pipeline run. which do you prefer?

anya: prefer to keep my PRs lightweight and not request maintainers each time. temporary PAT sounds fine for the initial runs.

lisa: created a masked pipeline var CI_GHCR_TOKEN for your buildkite pipeline with a scoped token (expires in 24h). re-run and let us know.

anya: re-ran, image pulled successfully and the build progressed :tada: thanks!

kevin: long-term we should: a) document the fork->CI flow in onboarding, b) make the runner image fall back to a public mirror on Docker Hub for forked PRs, and c) add a checklist item for accepting the GitHub App invite. i'll open an RFC to propose the fallback image and a tiny change in the pipeline to detect fork contexts.

rob: SGTM. also adding a short note to the onboarding playbook so new hires hit this less. thanks for the quick triage everyone.

anya: super helpful — appreciate the warm welcome! :smile:
